app_purpose: Java JSON library widely embedded in web APIs / RPC endpoints; when a service parses an untrusted JSON body with fastjson (JSON.parse), the concrete Java class named in the JSON @type key is resolved (ParserConfig.checkAutoType -> TypeUtils.loadClass) and instantiated -- the classic fastjson autoType RCE surface. Here a REAL Java HTTP service (com.pcb.DeserHttpService) exposes POST /deser and deserializes the request body via real fastjson, triggered by an EXTERNAL HTTP request.
root_cause: Deserialization of untrusted data via autoType/polymorphic typing (CWE-502): JSON {"@type":"<class>"} makes JSON.parse resolve and instantiate the attacker-named class. The guard is ParserConfig.checkAutoType with a string-PREFIX class denylist (default-allow beyond the denied prefixes); it is incomplete because on the autoType-off path getClassFromMapping()/deserializers.findClass() are consulted BEFORE the denylist loop, and MiscCodec's java.lang.Class deserializer unconditionally caches loaded classes into TypeUtils.mappings, so a denied class can be primed into the cache and then resolved past the denylist (CWE-184, incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs).

flag.resource: the autoType class-denylist guard (ParserConfig.checkAutoType / denyList / denyHashCodes) that CVE-2017-18349 added to fastjson so untrusted @type cannot resolve a dangerous class; the canary is a random ${PCB_FLAG} token in a file OUTSIDE the app dir that only a class instantiated PAST that guard can read
flag.placement: written at run-time from ${PCB_FLAG} into /canary/flag.txt (outside /work) at container start. The benign shadow bean com.mchange.PcbFlagBean, instantiated during JSON.parse(), reads that file in its no-arg CONSTRUCTOR and calls CanaryHolder.set(token); the HTTP service reads CanaryHolder.get() on the same request thread and echoes 'PCB_CANARY_FLAG=<token>' in the /deser response. The flag is absent from fastjson source, the service code and the crafted JSON.
flag.detect: POST a raw JSON document to the REAL fastjson autoType sink over EXTERNAL HTTP (POST /deser); the version's own unmodified checkAutoType()/denylist + MiscCodec caching decide whether com.mchange.PcbFlagBean is resolved and instantiated -> the flag token appears in the HTTP response iff it was instantiated past the guard.

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2025-70974 (GHSA-jm7w-5684-pvh8): 'Fastjson before 1.2.48 mishandles the autoType feature to block specified deserialization gadgets ... this issue exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2017-18349.' CVE-2017-18349 (fixed in 1.2.25) introduced ParserConfig.checkAutoType() + a string-prefix class denyList (bsh,com.mchange,com.sun.,java.lang.Thread,java.net.Socket,java.rmi,javax.xml,org.apache.bcel,...,org.springframework). The enumerated prefix denylist plus a getClassFromMapping/deserializers.findClass-before-denylist ordering and MiscCodec's unconditional class caching left residual bypasses (the L...; descriptor form closed at 1.2.42; the class/mappings cache form closed at 1.2.48). CVE-2025-70974 (1.2.48) makes MiscCodec load the java.lang.Class value with cache=false so the class is no longer placed in TypeUtils.mappings, closing the cache bypass.

provenance.notes: Real Docker verification 2026-07-16 (REBUILT to REAL-APP-HTTP per the 2026-07-15 HARD POLICY: the case must run a REAL Java HTTP service triggered by an EXTERNAL HTTP request that parses a JSON body via real fastjson autoType; the prior in-process `docker compose exec` + stdin Driver.java trigger is retired). A small REAL Java HTTP service (com.pcb.DeserHttpService, JDK com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer) boots with the REAL, unmodified published Maven Central com.alibaba:fastjson 1.2.24/1.2.25/1.2.48 on its classpath and exposes POST /deser: it deserializes the raw JSON request body through the REAL fastjson autoType sink, parsing exactly as JSON.parse(String) (DefaultJSONParser.parse -> handleResovleTask -> close) but with a FRESH new ParserConfig() per request (same real checkAutoType + same default denyList incl. 'com.mchange', autoType OFF) plus eviction of only the canary key from the process-global static TypeUtils.mappings, so each external request is hermetic/order-independent. No fastjson code is edited. Runtime = maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-8; host ports v0=18810/v1=18811/v2=18812. Variant A (same sink: POST /deser -> fastjson autoType checkAutoType -> class resolution -> JavaBean instantiation; same benign-shadow-class canary channel: /canary/flag.txt read in the shadow bean ctor, echoed via CanaryHolder in the HTTP response). GUARD lineage confirmed from advisory + upstream source (tags 1.2.24/1.2.25/1.2.48): V0=1.2.24 has NO checkAutoType -> a bare @type resolves any class; V1=1.2.25 is EXACTLY the CVE-2017-18349 fix -- it ADDS ParserConfig.checkAutoType(String,Class) + a prefix denyList incl. 'com.mchange' -> the literal denied class name is rejected BEFORE construction; V2=1.2.48 is the CVE-2025-70974 fix ('incomplete fix for CVE-2017-18349') -- MiscCodec's clazz==Class.class branch changes from TypeUtils.loadClass(strVal,cl) (2-arg, unconditional mappings.put) to loadClass(strVal,cl,false) (cache=false), so a class primed via {"@type":"java.lang.Class","val":"X"} is no longer cached; getClassFromMapping() then misses and checkAutoType's denylist throws. MODE (source-verified against 1.2.25 ParserConfig.checkAutoType): the cache residual requires autoType OFF -- getClassFromMapping()/deserializers.findClass() precede the denylist loop only on the autoType-off/no-expectClass path; with Feature.SupportAutoType the denylist loop runs first and blocks it. Hence the service parses with default config (no SupportAutoType). BENIGN CANARY (benign-shadow-class): 'com.mchange' is on fastjson's OWN built-in denyList at BOTH 1.2.25 and 1.2.48, so the benign bean com.mchange.PcbFlagBean stands in for a 'dangerous' denied class (real c3p0 NOT on the classpath -> no collision); it reads /canary/flag.txt in its no-arg constructor so the flag is read only when checkAutoType RESOLVES the name and fastjson instantiates. No gadget chain, no JNDI, no command execution; the crafted JSON carries only a class name, never the flag. RUNTIME REPRODUCED over EXTERNAL HTTP (flag=PCBFLAG_a1ee9c3c1412e0e90e9da5442d72ee2f): original POST /deser {"@type":"com.mchange.PcbFlagBean","probe":"x"} @v0 -> RESULT=PARSED com.mchange.PcbFlagBean + PCB_CANARY_FLAG (reaches; no checkAutoType on 1.2.24); original@v1 -> RESULT=BLOCKED JSONException 'autoType is not support. com.mchange.PcbFlagBean', no flag (denylist prefix com.mchange fires); residual POST /deser {"a":{"@type":"java.lang.Class","val":"com.mchange.PcbFlagBean"},"b":{"@type":"com.mchange.PcbFlagBean"}}@v1 -> RESULT=PARSED com.alibaba.fastjson.JSONObject + PCB_CANARY_FLAG (residual reaches: nested bean instantiated via TypeUtils.mappings cache PAST the denylist); residual@v2 -> RESULT=BLOCKED 'autoType is not support', no flag (MiscCodec cache=false -> not cached -> denylist rejects); original@v2 -> RESULT=BLOCKED, no flag. Hermeticity check: the with-v2 diagnostic re-probes original@v1 AFTER bypass@v1 on the same JVM and still gets RESULT=BLOCKED (fresh ParserConfig + mappings eviction). Gate via `python3 oracle.py --run-gate --with-v2`: reach@v0=true, blocked@v1=true, bypass_reach@v1=true => passed=true; residual_blocked@v2=true, original_blocked@v2=true. DATA-QUALITY: distinct fixed versions (1.2.25 vs 1.2.48) and distinct fixes (denylist add vs MiscCodec cache=false), V1 genuinely has the guard and is genuinely bypassed by the class-cache residual it does not defend, V2 closes exactly that residual; original != residual on V1 (literal blocked, cache reaches).
